बॉलीवु़ड के गलियारों से आ गई है एकदम तगड़ी और मसालेदार खबर! 🔥
रणबीर कपूर और यश स्टारर मचअवेटेड फिल्म Ramayana Part One को लेकर बॉक्स ऑफिस पर शुरुआती ट्रेंड्स सामने आ गए हैं।
रिपोर्ट्स के मुताबिक, यह फिल्म भारत में अपने पहले दिन करीब 65 करोड़ रुपये की बंपर कमाई करने की उम्मीद जता रही है।
इस माइथोलॉजिकल एपिक फिल्म में गुड वर्सेस ईविल की जंग दिखाई जाएगी, जिसे इंडियन सिनेमा के सबसे विजुअली स्टनिंग वेंचर्स में से एक बताया जा रहा है।
फैंस और सेलेब्स दोनों ही इस ग्रैंड प्रोजेक्ट को लेकर काफी ज्यादा एक्साइटेड नजर आ रहे हैं।
तो क्या आपने अपनी टिकट बुक कर ली है या आप पहले दिन का कलेक्शन देखने का इंतज़ार कर रहे हैं? 🎬✨

ctx.title: Ramayana Part One Early Box Office Trends: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash starrer looking to score Rs. 65 Cr first day in India
ctx.summary:
Ramayana: Part One is looking at a very good opening day of over Rs. 60 crore nett at the Indian box office. The Hindi version will likely be around Rs. 45 crore nett, while the South-dubbed versions are bringing in another Rs. 16-17 crore nett, led by Rs. 7.50-8 crore nett for the Kannada version. These numbers are exclusive of 3D charges, as has been the norm in India. However, the distribution is going to include 3D charges in its reporting, so the norm is probably finally going to change, as it should have from the start. Including 3D charges, first-day collections will be around Rs. 65 crore nett. 
 The film has performed better in South India, with Karnataka being the best. It will likely get close to Rs. 15 crore GROSS in the state, including 3D charges, which is a fantastic result. The presence of Kannada superstar Yash has played a part in that, but in general, the pre-Diwali period is less of a factor there, which meant the film managed to get closer to its potential.  
 The Hindi number will appear bad/disappointing, but that is down to the release timing, as the film is severely limited in the Hindi circuits, especially outside the metro centres. The film had a pre-sale of Rs. 23.50 crore nett at the start of the day, from which normally one would think of Rs. 55 crore or so day, but the walk-ups simply didn’t show up.
